discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computation and quantum simulation with trapped ions and ultracold atoms

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Innsbruck, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: Cirac and Zoller turned atomic physics into a platform for quantum information science. Their 1995 proposal of a quantum computer built from laser-cooled trapped ions gave the first realistic blueprint for entangling gates. It was quickly realized in experiments and still underlies today's ion-trap processors. Their 1998 proposal with Jaksch and others showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model. It predicted the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition, which was confirmed in 2002 and launched analog quantum simulation of many-body physics. Further concepts followed from them, including quantum repeaters, atom-light quantum interfaces, lattice gauge theories and topological phases with cold atoms. These have repeatedly set the agenda that experiments then confirmed. Their work joins quantum optics, condensed-matter physics and quantum information. It laid the conceptual groundwork for quantum simulators and quantum computers now built worldwide.
